title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 40
paragraphs: Now this Miltiades son of Cimon had at the time in question only recently returned to the Chersonese; and after his return there befell him other misfortunes worse than those he had already suffered. For two years before this he had been a fugitive from the land at the hands of the Scythians, since the nomad Scythians, provoked by King Darius, had joined together in a body and marched as far as this Chersonese; and Miltiades had not awaited their attack but had fled from the Chersonese, until at last the Scythians departed and the Dolonkians brought him back. These things had happened two years before the calamities that now oppressed him.
